about: The behavioural parity corpus for the bridge's VENDORED PHP copy of the coordination framework's Python PRIORITY-LANE rule (card#10273, adopting the primitive card#9936 / DL-414 built). The bridge cannot import Python, so it re-implements the rule; this file is the contract between the two copies, and it is RUNNABLE at both ends. Every entry is an ARGUMENT -> ANSWER pair, never a text comparison.

authority.relationship: The coordination framework OWNS this rule. The bridge mirrors it because it creates a coord card in real time (DL-198) and must place it in the lane the consumer's reconcile will agree with — on a board whose lane model is live, a create-time disagreement is not a placement but a REWRITE, and `user_lanes` then preserves whichever mover won. A disagreement is the bridge's defect to fix by re-mirroring.

how_the_far_end_runs_this: Run this repo's `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py --corpus docs/coord-lane-parity-corpus.json [--coord-examples <your templates/kanban/examples>]`. It binds the `coord` package to the directory named, so the scripts' own `from coord.kanban_common import …` resolves THERE and never to an installed copy elsewhere on `sys.path`; it refuses to measure (exit 2) if any `coord` function the scripts hold comes from a file outside that directory, and it prints the sha256 of every file it executed. It imports `_STAGE_LANE`, `_task_lane` and `classify_coord` FROM SOURCE and executes every vector below against them. SHAPE NOTES, both stated so a shape difference is never read as a drift: (1) the mirror's `resolveLane` answers `{lane, unmapped}` where the authority answers a lane NAME — the runner folds the mirror's null `lane` onto its `DEFAULT_LANE`, which is the lane the authority returns directly, and compares case-insensitively; `unmapped` is the mirror's own operator-warn material and has no far-end counterpart. (2) `governs` has no standalone callable at the far end — its gate lives inside `classify_coord` — so it is observed through the COLUMN `classify_coord` actually chooses for an issue carrying no `stage:*` label, where the lane branch lands on Later and every other open branch lands on Now or Awaiting ACK. That reads the real gate rather than a copy of its condition. `--control` perturbs every published expectation AND every pinned constant and requires each to be reported. Exit 0 = agreed, 1 = disagreed (a different answer, printed `DISAGREE:`, or the authority RAISED where this file records an answer, printed `RAISED:`), 2 = could not measure.
not_checked_by_this_repo: NOTHING HERE REDS WHEN THE COORDINATION FRAMEWORK CHANGES ITS OWN PYTHON. The far-end half is `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py`, deliberately NOT in this repo's CI, because CI has no copy of the authority. A green bridge suite says the mirror still answers what this file publishes — never that the authority still does.
Both arms are MEMBER-GRANULAR. A branch or an inline literal edited INSIDE an existing public method is outside both.

UNICODE CASE FOLDING IS A MEASURED DIVERGENCE and is pinned in `known_divergences`: Python's `str.upper()` is Unicode-aware and PHP's `strtoupper()` is ASCII-only, so a title whose uppercase form only BECOMES `[TASK]` under Unicode folding is lane-derived by the consumer and not by the bridge. It takes a deliberate homoglyph in an issue title to reach, and the consequence is one card created in the mapping's fixed stage instead of its declared lane.

THE LANE -> STAGE-ID HALF IS NOT MIRRORED AND IS NOT CHECKED HERE. The authority maps a lane to a stage EXTERNAL_ID (`LANE_TO_COLUMN`); the bridge maps it to a numeric stage id through operator config (`coord_card_lane_stage_ids`), because the `coordination.config.json` read that would let it derive the names is CLI-only. Nothing in this corpus says the two ends target the same physical column — only that they choose the same LANE.

`classify_coord`'s NON-`[TASK]` branches are out of scope and the mirror does not claim them. The authority sends a non-`[TASK]` open issue to Awaiting ACK when it is an announce and to Now otherwise; the bridge keeps the mapping's fixed `coord_card_stage_id`. That create disagreement PREDATES the lane model, is recorded in DL-286's sibling audit, and is not a drift in this mirror.
The measurement is against ONE version of the authority (`last_measured.authority_ref`). An install running a different coord version is UNMEASURED, not agreed.

last_measured.method: `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py --corpus docs/coord-lane-parity-corpus.json` executed every vector and every known divergence below against the authority named above, and held every constant against the authority's OWN data rather than against a copy: `LANES` against `_STAGE_LANE`'s values in its insertion order, `DEFAULT_LANE` against what `_task_lane` returns for an unlabelled issue, `LABEL_PREFIX` against the composition of `_STAGE_LANE`'s own keys, and `LANE_MODEL_TITLE_PREFIX` against whether `classify_coord` actually lane-derives a title carrying it (and does not, for one that does not). The same invocation with `--control` was run and reported EVERY perturbed expectation and EVERY perturbed pinned constant. Whoever adds, changes or DELETES a vector re-takes this measurement over the WHOLE corpus and rewrites `vectors_digest`; the bridge's own suite reds until they do.
last_measured.result: AGREED, AND THE ONE DISAGREEMENT IS NAMED RATHER THAN ABSENT. Every one of the 38 vectors and the 1 known divergence above was EXECUTED against the authority named in `authority_ref`, and every constant was held against the authority's own `_STAGE_LANE` / `_task_lane` / `classify_coord` rather than against a copy; all agreed. The run is falsifiable: the same command with `--control` perturbed every expectation and every pinned constant, and reported every one. ⚠ THIS IS A DATED OBSERVATION OF ONE AUTHORITY VERSION, NOT A STANDING PROPERTY — nothing in the bridge's CI re-takes it, because CI has no copy of the authority.

not_mirrored.LANE_TO_COLUMN / USER_LANES: The authority's lane -> stage-external-id map and its curated-lane set. The bridge reaches stage ids through operator config instead — see `not_checked_by_this_repo`.
not_mirrored._itype and the announce branch: `classify_coord`'s non-`[TASK]` routing. Deliberately not mirrored; see `not_checked_by_this_repo`.

governs.why: UNICODE CASE FOLDING. `'[TAſK] x'.upper()` is `'[TASK] X'` in Python (U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S folds to ASCII 'S'), so the authority lane-derives it; PHP's `strtoupper()` is ASCII-only and leaves the byte alone, so the mirror does not. Measured 2026-09-24. The mirror is the one that is arguably wrong here — its contract is 'the set of issues the CONSUMER lane-derives' — but correcting it changes what the bridge creates, which card#10273 puts out of scope; it is pinned so that a later `mb_strtoupper` fix reds this entry instead of passing unnoticed.

governs.note: the ordinary shape: the anchored title prefix the authority gates the lane model on.
LOWERCASE: both ends uppercase the title before the anchored match.

a LEADING SPACE is not the prefix. NEGATIVE — and deliberately unlike `CoordinationClassifier::stableId()`, which trims before its own anchored match: this gate's contract is the set of issues the CONSUMER lane-derives, not the set the bridge cards.
another coordination prefix is not governed. NEGATIVE.
an announce is not governed — the authority sends it to Awaiting ACK, which this mirror does not claim. NEGATIVE.
the prefix and nothing else still governs — `startswith` / `str_starts_with`, not a word match.
the prefix ANYWHERE BUT THE START does not govern. NEGATIVE — this is what 'anchored' buys.
a LONGER prefix does NOT match, because the closing bracket is part of the token. NEGATIVE, and the one most likely to be mis-mirrored by someone matching '[TASK' instead.
no separator needed after the bracket — the rule is a prefix test, and both ends agree on the same surprising answer.

isLaneLabel.note: the ordinary shape: a label naming a lane of the model.
each lane of the model in turn — `next`.
UPPERCASE: both ends lowercase before testing.
MIXED CASE, the shape a hand-edit actually produces.

THE PREFIX ALONE IS NOT THE QUESTION. `stage:done` is in the `stage:` namespace and states no lane this model knows. NEGATIVE — and the one that makes this a behaviour difference rather than a tidiness one (card#6393): a MOVE keyed on the prefix would demote a card to `later` on a label that expressed no lane.
the bare prefix names no lane. NEGATIVE.
a lane name WITHOUT the prefix. NEGATIVE.
the prefix must be at the START. NEGATIVE.
the lane must be the WHOLE remainder, not a prefix of it. NEGATIVE.

resolveLane.note: the ordinary shape: one declared lane, mapped.
NO `stage:*` label at all — the mirror answers null and the caller lands on DEFAULT_LANE, which is exactly what the authority returns. NEGATIVE.
TWO declared lanes resolve in `_STAGE_LANE`'s insertion order, NOT the label order — which is what makes a multi-labelled issue land in the same lane on both movers.
a declared lane the board does not carry is SKIPPED, and with nothing else declared the scan is exhausted.

THE LOAD-BEARING VECTOR for where the availability test sits: INSIDE the loop. Testing it after the loop — resolve first, then fall back — would answer `later` here and `Next` there, a create-time disagreement `user_lanes` then preserves.
the scan CONTINUES past an unmapped lane to a later one in model order, rather than stopping at the first declared lane.
several declared, one mapped, and the mapped one is not the first in model order. Note `maybe` is NOT reported unmapped — the scan returns before reaching it, on both ends.
an UNRECOGNISED `stage:*` label declares no lane and is not reported as unmapped either. NEGATIVE.
`stage:done` — in the namespace, not of the model. NEGATIVE.
labels are lowercased on both ends, so a hand-edited `Stage:Now` still resolves.
the same, uppercased on the lane rather than the prefix.
the last lane in model order, on a board mapping only it.
`later` declared EXPLICITLY resolves as a lane — distinct from `later` reached as the default, which the two vectors above cover.
a board mapping NO lanes at all: everything falls to the default. NEGATIVE.
model order again, with the labels supplied in the reverse of it.
